cells.tense: Right now, something has run its course and the leaving of it is already underway.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Let your practice move both ways this week — help offered, help taken — without keeping count of either.
cells.core:
You can end a thing when it has actually ended. That is a rarer skill than starting one. Where you keep your practice, you notice what has finished, you let it finish, and you don't drag the husk along with you. Because you go by what you feel rather than what you fear, the cleanup is quiet and usually right-sized.

What keeps this clean is that it stays even. Some of what moves is given out, some is let in, and both directions stay open. An uneven exchange, even a generous one, wears a person down slowly, and your practice is the first place you would feel that. Keep both ways open and the ending stays easy to do.
cells.sheetLine: You end what has ended, and the next thing has room.
cells.verb: ending what has finished so what comes next can start
cells.place: the daily practice kept by repetition, where the small steady light is tended

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead, endings are already being lined up and rehearsed before anything has finished living.
cells.act: stay in contact while it is hard
cells.ask: Stay in contact with the difficult thing one week past where you would usually cut it — one more session, one more unhurried conversation — before deciding anything.
cells.core:
Out ahead of yourself, endings happen early. Things get cleared before they have lived, and that reads as liberation right up until you notice how much you keep having to clear. That is the shape of it: motion that looks like release and is really bracing, because the next loss is already being prepared for.

Staying is the plainer move. Not forever — a week past where you would usually go. Stay in contact with the difficult thing while it is still hard, without fixing it or yourself. Whatever is actually finished will still be finished after the week. Whatever is not will tell you so, in a way you can feel rather than decide.
cells.sheetLine: You end things early, so nothing gets to prove itself.
cells.verb: ending what has finished so what comes next can start

cells.tense: A door is behind you now and your hand has not moved off it.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Follow the pull that is already there — a step in a direction that has been tugging at you, small enough that getting it wrong costs nothing.
cells.core:
Where you practice, everything is kept exactly as it was. The motions are the same ones, repeated, and repetition has quietly become preservation. Nothing here is being refined toward anything anymore; it is being kept alive by habit. That steadiness is real, and from inside it, it doesn't feel like fear. Whether it is loyalty or stalling, you are the one who would know.

Momentum moves through the practice. Follow a pull that is already there, before you feel ready — a direction that has been tugging at you, small enough that getting it wrong costs nothing. Effort aimed straight at the stuck place won't do it. What is finished can rest once something else has your feet, and something already does.
cells.sheetLine: You are tending something that finished, and calling it loyalty.
cells.verb: ending what has finished so what comes next can start

cells.tense: You are already letting something go, and you would not say so if asked.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: Build the smallest shape around it — a start, a stop, an order — and set that where you will see it. No fixing, no one told.
cells.core:
Somewhere in you, something is ending, and the ending is happening without your hand on it. You practice, and the practice holds. Whatever is passing is not being marked as passing. From the outside, others can likely see it; from yours, this is simply how things are, and there is nothing to report.

Naming it changes nothing about the ending, only about who is doing it. Build the smallest shape around it — a start, a stop, an order — and set that where you will see it. No fixing, and no one has to be told. Once it has a shape, the leaving is something you are choosing rather than something landing on you, which is the difference between being carried and walking.
cells.sheetLine: What is leaving you is leaving, and you didn't say so.
